Give your AI agents the power to see, build, and render in 3D. 🤖✨

Meet Vork: a headless 3D and VFX rendering engine written in Rust and Slang, built specifically for AI agents to write, render, and refine scenes without human-driven editors.

The Problem:
Integrating high-end 3D graphics and VFX into autonomous AI workflows has always hit a massive bottleneck. Traditional pipelines require GUI editors operated by humans. Vork solves this by exposing geometry, ray queries, and GPU execution directly to code.

Why developers are building with Vork:
⚡ Headless Architecture: Powered by Rust, Vulkan, and Metal with high-end GPU ray queries and zero GUI required.
🤖 First-Class Agent Integration: CLI commands, JSON schemas, and structured help tooling built explicitly for AI consumption and iterative self-correction.
🔥 Slang Compute Programs: Advanced custom shaders and simulation capabilities allowing agents to implement complex physics, fluids, and custom light propagation.
🎬 Advanced Scene Composition: Supports standalone 3D generation and advanced VFX compositing straight onto real-world video footage.

Stop relying on unpredictable generative video models. Give your agents deterministic 3D control to simulate physics, handle lighting, and iterate on cinematic shots entirely through code.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/voyager-so/vork

Drop a comment if you are building autonomous creative agents, and star the repo to support open-source AI infrastructure! 👇

Bring interactive 2.5D web avatars and VTuber-style streaming directly to the browser using a lightweight, dependency-free WebGL2 player! 🚀

Tired of the complexity and heavy resource requirements of traditional desktop VTuber and character runtimes? 

LivLiv Player is a lightweight, dependency-free WebGL2 JavaScript library that renders 2.5D characters, VRM models, and PNGTubers natively in the browser with real-time lip sync and webcam face tracking. 💡

✨ Key Features:
• Featherlight Core: ~30 KB gzipped with zero runtime dependencies and built entirely on WebGL2.
• Real-Time Tracking & Audio: Client-side real-time lip sync supporting mic/audio/video inputs and in-browser webcam face tracking powered by Google MediaPipe.
• Unified API: Render LivLiv packages, VRM avatars via Three.js, and classic PNGTubers interchangeably.
• Out-of-the-Box Ready: Comprehensive support for expressions, skeletal actions, and 21 pre-styled featured characters.

🛠️ Why Developers Love It:
Gain a drop-in ES module solution to embed expressive, responsive characters into web apps or OBS browser sources with just a few lines of JavaScript. By executing MediaPipe and audio analysis locally in the user's browser, it completely bypasses heavy server-side processing to significantly cut down infrastructure costs and latency.

🌐 Perfect for building browser-based VTuber stream overlays for OBS or adding interactive virtual assistant and mascot widgets to web applications.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/livliv-dev/player

Tired of heavy local container environments? 🚀

Say goodbye to the massive RAM overhead, sluggish startup times, and battery drain of traditional tools. Meet Kiri, a tiny, memory-safe Rust container runtime that boots up containers 80 times faster than Docker Desktop.

Written completely in Rust, Kiri bypasses heavy layers like dockerd, runc, and shims using a custom 10 MB kernel and a lean guest agent. The best part? It speaks the standard Docker Engine API, meaning it works out of the box with your existing Docker CLI, Compose, and buildx workflows without changing your habits.

🔥 Key Features:
• Blazing fast: Spin up and tear down containers via the Docker API in approximately 2.5 milliseconds.
• Featherlight footprint: The daemon rests at around 15 MB, and the underlying VM goes to sleep after 60 seconds of idle time with sub-second wake times.
• Developer-first utilities: Get local wildcard domains with custom certificates, single-command Kubernetes clusters, and standalone Linux machines out of the box.

Whether you are running multi-container microservice stacks locally via Docker Compose or spinning up quick, disposable K8s clusters, Kiri gives you a lightning-fast, battery-friendly alternative that saves your laptop's resources.

Check out the repository and try it today:
https://github.com/libracoder/kiri

Tired of rigid screen-time timers that just teach kids how to bypass them? Turn your household Android TVs and tablets into interactive learning stations instead.

Meet StudyOnTV: An open-source, offline-first Android app that forces kids to solve educational questions to unlock screen time. No external cloud servers, no third-party tracking, and zero subscriptions—just pure local-first digital wellbeing.

Here is why developers and tech-savvy parents are loving it:

⚡ Zero-Dependency Native Android Stack: Built entirely in Kotlin with zero third-party dependencies, running an embedded HTTP server via a raw ServerSocket on port 8099 to serve the admin dashboard locally.
📱 Dual-Layer Client Architecture: Features a lightweight learning interface optimized for older WebViews alongside a modern React and shadcn/ui management dashboard accessible instantly via a local LAN QR code scan.
🧠 EdTech & AI Grading Engine: Supports LaTeX math, handwriting, voice input, spaced repetition, and subjective AI grading via integrated endpoints like DeepSeek, Ollama, and custom agents.
🔒 Robust Local Resilience: Leverages built-in Android SQLite for storing rules, question banks, and audit logs locally, ensuring absolute privacy and continuity even across device reboots and network drops.

For Android developers and full-stack hobbyists, this codebase is an incredible reference implementation. It shows how to bridge low-level Android components like system audio focus, boot receivers, and kiosk-like restrictions directly with an embedded web server and native SQLite persistence—all without heavy ORMs.

Ready to check out the code or deploy it to your home devices? 

Explore the repository here:
https://github.com/chadyi/StudyOnTV

Tired of LLMs choking on verbose Blender scripts and complex coordinate matrices when trying to generate 3D assets? 

Meet Sand3d (https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d), a game-changing Python library that bridges the gap between text-to-CAD and programmatic 3D generation. Built on Blender's bpy module, it replaces heavy GUI workflows with a concise vocabulary where 3D objects are defined as short, declarative code blocks.

Here is why AI and robotics engineers are adding it to their stack:

✨ Ultra Token-Efficient API: The entire API fits into ~3,600 tokens—consuming 2x to 6x fewer tokens per part than standard Blender Python or CadQuery. Perfect for fitting directly into LLM system prompts.
🏷️ Named Geometry & Topology: Parts, edges, and faces are addressed by semantic names instead of fragile, hand-computed coordinate matrices, virtually eliminating spatial reasoning errors.
🤖 First-Class Articulation: Explicitly handles hierarchical groups, moving parts, and kinematic joints (continuous, prismatic, hinge) for complex assemblies.
🔄 Comprehensive Exports: Export directly to GLB for web, URDF for ROS and physics simulators like Isaac and PyBullet, OpenUSD (USDA), OBJ, and STL.

Whether you are building text-to-CAD generative pipelines, automated simulation environments, or procedural asset libraries, Sand3d bypasses the fragility of direct mesh generation to output production-grade files.

Check out the repository, drop a star, and start building your automated 3D pipelines today:
https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d
